fit22<- cfa(model222,data=carpatos ,std.lv=T,estimator="mlmv")

I have the issue after i do the fit22. It says

Error in lavData(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster, ov.names = ov.names,  :

When i use sample.cov instead of data:

Any comment, let me know.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: error lavaan WARNING: data argument looks like a covariance matrix; please use the sample.cov
parts:
You have 129 observed variables in the model and 129 cases or observations? You can't hope for much in such a case, but the WARNING may have been promoted because your data rectangle is square--129 x 129. Still, that is just a warning--if you know everything is "OK," then ignore it.
     In the second case, that is an ERROR, and you have to do something about it. When you use summary moments (like a covariance matrix) as input, you must specify sample size, because the program has no way to tell.
     Again, granting the shortcomings of your sample size, you can ignore the WARNING.

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: error lavaan WARNING: data argument looks like a covariance matrix; please use the sample.cov
parts:
Jose,
This is to confirm Ed's interpretation of the warning with a twist.  The warning is generated by a hidden function called lavData().

...
 if (!is.null(data)) {
        if (inherits(data, "lavData")) {
            return(data)
        }
        else if (inherits(data, "lavaan")) {
            return(data@Data)
        }
        if (!is.data.frame(data)) {
            if (is.matrix(data)) {
                if (nrow(data) == ncol(data)) {
                  stop("lavaan WARNING: data argument looks like a covariance matrix; please use the sample.cov argument instead")
                }
...

As you can see, the warning is generated any time the input matrix is not null, not a data frame, a matrix, and square.  This suggests that your data set is not a data frame but is a matrix.  So, you could try replacing your data matrix with a data frame to eliminate the warning.

myDataFrame <- as.data.frame(myDataMatrix)

Keith
